- Overestimate prices when sentiment is positive and recent highs are followed by a spike; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% after a sharp upward move.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or shows early signs of decline; add 3–5% to forecast to compensate for downward bias.
- Forecast tends to lag behind true price movements by 2–4 days; adjust forward by 1–2 days if sentiment is trending upward.
- Mean reversion is strong in early 2025 data; if forecast is above 75% of recent 10-day average, reduce by 2–5% unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
- Overshoots occur after sentiment spikes; cap forecast at 10% above recent 5-day high if sentiment > 0.65.
- If sentiment is below 0.30 for 3+ consecutive days, reduce forecast by 3–7% to avoid overconfidence in downward momentum.
- Forecast should not exceed 10% above the 30-day moving average unless sentiment is > 0.70 and price is trending upward.
